pr_title: Update zwave_js supported features list to be static
pr_body:
## Proposed change
The supported features property returns a different list depending on the current HVAC mode. This change makes the supported features list static.

QUESTION: In the linked issue, Martin mentioned that attributes should be `None` when appropriate. Should target_temp_low and high be `None` when the thermostat is in heat_cool mode? Right now, low will have the same value as target_temperature and high will be None in those cases. Similarly, when we are on heat_cool, target temperature will have a value even as target_temp_high and low have values

Hey there @home-assistant/z-wave, mind taking a look at this pull request as its been labeled with an integration (`zwave_js`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L556) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Either `target_temperature` or `target_temperature_low` and `target_temperature_high` should return something other `None`. Low and high are inclusive to each other and exclusive to `target_temperature`.

> Either `target_temperature` or `target_temperature_low` and `target_temperature_high` should return something other `None`. Low and high are inclusive to each other and exclusive to `target_temperature`.

OK, I know what to do here for `heat`, `cool`, and `heat_cool`, what about `fan_only`, `dry`, `auto`, and `off`?  I'm assuming `auto` is like `heat_cool`, do the others not have a target temperature at all?

> > Either `target_temperature` or `target_temperature_low` and `target_temperature_high` should return something other `None`. Low and high are inclusive to each other and exclusive to `target_temperature`.
> 
> OK, I know what to do here for `heat`, `cool`, and `heat_cool`, what about `fan_only`, `dry`, `auto`, and `off`? I'm assuming `auto` is like `heat_cool`, do the others not have a target temperature at all?

`auto` doesn't apply since we don't use it, but we do support the other three

> > Either `target_temperature` or `target_temperature_low` and `target_temperature_high` should return something other `None`. Low and high are inclusive to each other and exclusive to `target_temperature`.
> 
> OK, I know what to do here for `heat`, `cool`, and `heat_cool`, what about `fan_only`, `dry`, `auto`, and `off`? I'm assuming `auto` is like `heat_cool`, do the others not have a target temperature at all?

I don't think we have standardized that. The frontend will show the temperature controls if the temperature attributes are not None and the correct supported features are set, as far as I know.

The only rule we have is for auto, where the user shouldn't be able to change temperature.

> 
> 
> > > Either `target_temperature` or `target_temperature_low` and `target_temperature_high` should return something other `None`. Low and high are inclusive to each other and exclusive to `target_temperature`.
> > 
> > 
> > OK, I know what to do here for `heat`, `cool`, and `heat_cool`, what about `fan_only`, `dry`, `auto`, and `off`? I'm assuming `auto` is like `heat_cool`, do the others not have a target temperature at all?
> 
> `auto` doesn't apply since we don't use it, but we do support the other three

What about the AUTO_CHANGEOVER mode? It is currently mapped to heat_cool, which requires two setpoints. AUTO_CHANGEOVER uses a single setpoint.

issue_context.title: Homekit Thermostat Auto mode not displaying min and max temperature range
issue_context.body:
### The problem

With the old native ZWave integration in Home Assistant core you were able to go the home app and set your thermostat to auto and the home app would display a min/max for your temperature range. The thermostat behind the scenes, was a zwave thermostat exposed to homekit by home assistant. After moving to OZW and now still present in ZWaveJS the thermostat in homekit when in mode auto only shows a set temperature rather than a range.

I posted this post on the community forum but not sure if anyone else is facing this issue. I can't test this with a different kind of thermostat as I don't have another zwave thermostat. However, it was working and my thermostat has stayed connected to my ZWave stick since the old native ZWave integration.

https://community.home-assistant.io/t/homekit-climate-not-able-to-set-both-min-and-max-temp-using-ozw/226612

### What is version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2021.3.0

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

0.112

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant Core

### Integration causing the issue

Homekit

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/homekit/

### Example YAML snippet

```yaml
# Put your YAML below this line

```


### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
# Put your logs below this line

```


This is how the climate entity exposed by Home Assistant Core via Homekit from ZWave displays when in `auto` mode. It should and use to show a range for the temperature range.

comments:
Hey there @bdraco, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`homekit`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L201) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>
HomeKit can only work with the data that is provided to it. Since it was working with old zwave, that means that its likely not going though with `zwave_js`.

Hey there @home-assistant/z-wave, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`zwave_js`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L556) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

> HomeKit can only work with the data that is provided to it. Since it was working with old zwave, that means that its likely not going though with `zwave_js`.

Just so I understand you mean to say that you suspect the integration with ZWave JS may not be feeding the data to the HomeKit integration that it needs in order for the auto mode to work properly? Is this UI suspicion?

It looks like for `zwave`, `SUPPORT_TARGET_TEMPERATURE` is always enabled and `SUPPORT_TARGET_TEMPERATURE_RANGE` is enabled if auto is in the available HVAC modes. `ozw` and `zwave_js` selectively only enable `SUPPORT_TARGET_TEMPERATURE` if the HVAC is actively in heat/cool mode and `SUPPORT_TARGET_TEMPERATURE_RANGE` if the HVAC is actively in auto mode. My guess is that homekit integration requires those to always be set, which is the case for `zwave` but not for `ozw` or `zwave_js`. @bdraco does that sound right in terms of what homekit expects from a supported_features perspective?

Assuming I am correct, the question is what should the right behavior be? In testing, if we use the `zwave` approach, the entity state will always have attributes for `target_temperature`, `target_temperature_high`, `target_temperature_low`, including during times where those attributes aren't relevant. Is that really what we want?

> `ozw` and `zwave_js` selectively only enable `SUPPORT_TARGET_TEMPERATURE` if the HVAC is actively in heat/cool mode and `SUPPORT_TARGET_TEMPERATURE_RANGE` if the HVAC is actively in auto mode. 

HomeKit definitely doesn't except the device to change its supported feature set based on the state its in.  It is expecting that `supported_features` remains stable.

In case its helpful.  Here is how we handle low temp, high temp, or temp with `nexia`

https://github.com/bdraco/nexia/blob/master/nexia/zone.py#L262

The supported features should be set based on the total features of the device. This shouldn't change during entity lifetime. The temperature properties should return `None` when they are not relevant for the current mode. So that can change during the entity lifetime.
OK i have a PR ready to handle this for `zwave_js`, will submit it soon

review_comments: Is it possible to know at init time how many setpoints each possible mode provides, ie if there's a high and a low setpoint for that mode or just a single temperature setpoint?

yes, the `THERMOSTAT_MODE_SETPOINT_MAP` constant in the library maps `ThermostatMode` to a setpoint list, and `ZW_HVAC_MODE_MAP` in HA maps `ThermostatMode` to an HA mode. So we could work backwards to map HA mode to setpoint list. Is the thought that we rely on that to determine which targets to show?

Yes, we want to show high and low target temp if the mode has the two corresponding setpoints but only target temp if the mode only has one setpoint. Looks like it's only `ThermostatMode.AUTO` and `ThermostatMode.AWAY` that have two setpoints.
So the current solution is already correct.
uhh I don't think it is based on that statement. low will have always have a value with this implementation.
Ok, but we don't set supported features to range unless there's a mode with two setpoints. So that part is correct.
I mean this PR is correct. We can address the temperature attributes separately if needed.
